sentences.chinese: 」不答。
sentences.literal: Closing the quoted memorial—no reply was issued.
sentences.idiomatic: The court returned no answer.

sentences.chinese: 十八年，胤又上言：「去年上，自頃開國公侯，至於卿士，庶子為後者，服其庶母，同之於嫡，違禮犯制，宜加裁抑。
sentences.literal: In the eighteenth year, Yin again submitted words: "Last year I submitted—since recently founding-state dukes and marquises down to ministers and gentlemen—those secondary sons who become heirs—they observe mourning for their secondary mothers—as equal to the principal mother—violating ritual and infringing regulation—fitting to add curbing restraint.
sentences.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, Yin again memorialized: "My petition last year noted that, from the founding ranks onward—dukes and marquises down to senior officials—heirs born of secondary consorts have been mourning their birth mothers on the same footing as a principal mother. That breaches canonical mourning law and ought to be restrained.

sentences.chinese: 事上經年，未被告報，未審朝議以何為疑。
sentences.literal: The matter has been on file a full year—yet no notification has come—I do not know what doubt the court deliberation harbors.
sentences.idiomatic: A year has passed since it went up, yet no ruling has come down; I cannot tell what hesitation keeps the council silent.

sentences.chinese: 若以所陳或謬，則經有文；
sentences.literal: If because what was stated perhaps errs—then the classics have the wording;
sentences.idiomatic: If my argument is mistaken, the canon itself supplies the text;

sentences.chinese: 若以古今不同，則晉有成典。
sentences.literal: If because ancient and present differ—then Jin has established precedent.
sentences.idiomatic: If the objection is that antiquity and today diverge, Jin already has binding precedent.

sentences.chinese: 升平四年，故太宰武陵王所生母喪，表求齊衰三年，詔聽依昔樂安王故事，制大功九月。
sentences.literal: In the fourth year of Shengping—the late Grand Tutor Prince of Wuling's birth mother died—he memorialized requesting zīcuī for three years—the edict permitted him to follow the former Prince of Le'an precedent—regulating greater felicitous mourning at nine months.
sentences.idiomatic: In Shengping 4, when the birth mother of the late Grand Tutor, the Prince of Wuling, died, he petitioned for three years in trimmed sackcloth; the throne allowed him to follow the old Prince of Le'an precedent and fixed greater mourning at nine months.

sentences.chinese: ，故梁王㻱又所生母喪，亦求三年。
sentences.literal: —therefore when the Prince of Liang, Jin, lost his birth mother—he too requested three years.
sentences.idiomatic: Likewise, when the Prince of Liang, Jin, lost his birth mother, he too sought three full years.

sentences.chinese: 《庚子詔書》依太宰故事，同服大功。
sentences.literal: The Gēngzǐ Edict Document followed the Grand Tutor precedent—likewise prescribing greater felicitous mourning.
sentences.idiomatic: The Gēngzǐ edict followed the Grand Tutor precedent and likewise prescribed nine months of greater mourning.

sentences.chinese: 若謹案周禮，則緦麻三月；
sentences.literal: If one carefully examines the Rites of Zhou—then finest hemp is three months;
sentences.idiomatic: Strictly applying the Zhou canon would mean only three months in finest hemp;

sentences.chinese: 若奉晉制，則大功九月。
sentences.literal: If one upholds Jin's regulation—then greater felicitous mourning is nine months.
sentences.idiomatic: Under Jin's own statute, it is nine months of greater mourning.

sentences.chinese: 古禮今制，並無居廬三年之文，而頃年已來，各申私情，更相擬襲，漸以成俗。
sentences.literal: Ancient ritual and present regulation together lack any text authorizing three years in the mourning hut—yet in recent years already come—each voices private feeling—mutually imitating and inheriting—gradually thereby becoming custom.
sentences.idiomatic: Neither classical ritual nor current codes authorize three years in the mourning hut; yet lately everyone pleads private feeling, copies one another, and the practice is hardening into habit.

sentences.chinese: 縱而不禁，則聖典滅矣。
sentences.literal: If indulged and not forbidden—then the sagely canon is extinguished.
sentences.idiomatic: If we indulge it and never curb it, the sagely canon will be hollowed out.

sentences.chinese: 夫尊尊親親，立人之本，王化所由，二端而已。
sentences.literal: Now honoring the honored and cherishing the cherished—establishing people's root—kingly transformation whereby—it is these two ends only.
sentences.idiomatic: Reverence for rank and affection for kin are the twin foundations of human order and the springs of royal transformation—nothing beyond these two.

sentences.chinese: 故先王設教，務弘其極，尊郊社之敬，制越紼之禮，嚴宗廟之祀，厭庶子之服，所以經緯人文，化成天下。
sentences.literal: Therefore former kings established teaching—striving to enlarge its utmost—honoring reverence for the suburban and soil altars—regulating the ritual of vaulting the funeral cords—strictening ancestral temple sacrifices—suppressing what secondary heirs may wear for birth parents—thereby warp-and-wefting human patterns—transforming and completing all under heaven.
sentences.idiomatic: Hence the ancient kings framed instruction to carry each principle to its limit: they magnified reverence for suburban and soil altars, set rules for vaulting the funeral cords, tightened ancestral worship, and bridled what secondary heirs might wear for birth parents—thus ordering civilization's warp and weft until the realm was shaped.

sentences.chinese: 夫屈家事于王道，厭私恩於祖宗，豈非上行乎下，父行乎子！
sentences.literal: Now bending family affairs to the kingly way—suppressing private grace toward ancestors—is this not the high acting upon the low—the father acting upon the son!
sentences.idiomatic: To subordinate household sentiment to the kingly norm and set private tenderness beneath ancestral duty—is that not precisely how what is high trains what is low, and fathers train sons?

sentences.chinese: 若尊尊之心有時而替，宜厭之情觸事而申，祖宗之敬微，而君臣之禮虧矣。
sentences.literal: If the mind that honors hierarchy falters at times—while the feeling fit for suppression swells whenever affairs arise—reverence for ancestors grows subtle—then the ritual between lord and minister is impaired.
sentences.idiomatic: Once reverence for hierarchy falters and disciplined restraint swells at every turn of feeling, respect for forebears thins and the ritual bond between ruler and minister erodes.

sentences.chinese: 嚴恪微於祖宗，致敬虧於事上，而欲俗安化隆，不亦難乎！
sentences.literal: Strict reverence toward ancestors grows subtle—extended reverence toward serving superiors is impaired—yet one desires customs pacified and transformation lofty—is this not difficult!
sentences.idiomatic: When solemn duty toward the ancestors fades and dutiful deference to superiors frays, can customs settle and transformation flourish? Surely that is hard.

sentences.chinese: 區區所惜，實在於斯。
sentences.literal: What I regret in my meager way truly lies in this.
sentences.idiomatic: What troubles me, slight though my voice may be, is precisely this.

sentences.chinese: 職之所司，不敢不言。
sentences.literal: What my office oversees—I dare not fail to speak.
sentences.idiomatic: The office I hold leaves me no silence.

sentences.chinese: 請臺參詳。
sentences.literal: I request the terrace offices to deliberate in detail.
sentences.idiomatic: I ask the supreme departments to deliberate.

sentences.chinese: 」尚書奏：「案如辭輒下主者詳尋。
sentences.literal: The Secretariat memorialized: "Investigate as the wording states—then dispatch it to the responsible overseers for thorough inquiry.
sentences.idiomatic: The Secretariat reported: "As the wording requests, forward this at once to the responsible offices for thorough inquiry.

sentences.chinese: 依禮，庶子與尊者為體，不敢服其私親，此尊祖敬宗之義。
sentences.literal: According to ritual, the secondary son shares one body with the exalted predecessor—he dares not observe mourning for his private kin—this is the meaning of honoring ancestors and revering the main line.
sentences.idiomatic: By ritual a secondary heir shares one body with his exalted predecessor and therefore does not wear mourning for his own birth parent—that is how one honors forebears and reveres the main line.

sentences.chinese: 自頃陵遲，斯禮遂廢。
sentences.literal: Since recently standards have declined—this ritual has then been abandoned.
sentences.idiomatic: Of late, as standards slackened, that rule fell away.

sentences.chinese: 封國之君廢五廟之重，士庶匹夫闕烝嘗之禮，習成穨俗，宜被革正。
sentences.literal: Lords of enfeoffed states abandon the weight of the five temples—gentlemen and commoners lack the steam-and-taste offerings—practice completes a decadent custom—fitting that it receive reform and correction.
sentences.idiomatic: Feudal lords neglect the gravity of the five shrines; commoners omit seasonal offerings at home—habit has rotted into custom and ought to be cleaned up.

sentences.chinese: 輒內外參詳，謂宜聽胤所上，可依樂安王大功為正。
sentences.literal: We have consulted inside and outside—we deem it fitting to accept what Yin submitted—one may rely on the Prince of Le'an's greater felicitous mourning as standard.
sentences.idiomatic: After consulting court and ministries, we hold that Yin's petition should be accepted and the Prince of Le'an precedent—nine months of greater mourning—should be taken as normative.

sentences.chinese: 請為告書如左，班下內外，以定永制，普令依承，事可奉行。
sentences.literal: We request drafting a proclamation document as at left—distributing it through court and countryside—to fix a perpetual regulation—universally ordering compliance—so the affair may be enacted and followed.
sentences.idiomatic: We ask that an edict be drafted along the lines below, circulated through court and countryside to settle the standing rule, enjoin universal compliance, and put the matter into practice.

sentences.chinese: 」詔可。
sentences.literal: The edict approved.
sentences.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.chinese: 《禮》，王為三公六卿錫衰，為大夫士疑衰，首服弁絰。
sentences.literal: The Canon of Rites: the king wears smooth sackcloth for the Three Dukes and the six ministers, doubtful sackcloth for great officers and gentlemen, with cap and forehead cord as headgear.
sentences.idiomatic: The Canon of Rites prescribes that the king wear smooth sackcloth for the Three Dukes and six ministers, doubtful sackcloth for great officers and gentlemen, with cap and forehead cord.

sentences.chinese: 天子諸侯皆為貴臣貴妾服三月。
sentences.literal: Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike observe three months' mourning for honored ministers and honored concubines.
sentences.idiomatic: Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike observe three months' mourning for favored ministers and favored concubines.

sentences.chinese: 漢為大臣制服無聞焉。
sentences.literal: For Han, regulating mourning garments for great ministers—nothing is heard of it.
sentences.idiomatic: Han sources record no fixed mourning wardrobe for great ministers.

sentences.chinese: 漢明帝時，東海恭王薨，帝出幸津門亭發哀。
sentences.literal: In the time of Han Mingdi, the Respectful Prince of the Eastern Sea died—the emperor went out to the Ferry Gate pavilion to voice grief.
sentences.idiomatic: Under Han Mingdi, when the Respectful Prince of the Eastern Sea died, the emperor travelled to the Ferry Gate pavilion to voice grief.

sentences.chinese: 及武帝十一月，詔「諸王公大臣薨，應三朝發哀者，逾月不舉樂，其一朝發哀者，三日不舉樂也」。
sentences.literal: When it came to Emperor Wu, in the eleventh month, an edict declared: "When various kings, dukes, and great ministers die—those who ought to observe mourning at three successive audiences—for more than a month they shall not raise music—those who observe mourning at one audience—for three days they shall not raise music."
sentences.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Emperor Wu's reign an edict declared: "When kings, dukes, or senior ministers die, those who observe mourning at three successive audiences shall refrain from music for more than a month; those who mourn at only one audience shall refrain for three days."

sentences.chinese: 元帝姨廣昌鄉君喪，未葬，中丞熊遠表云：「案《禮》『君于卿大夫，比葬不食肉，比卒哭不舉樂』，惻隱之心未忍行吉事故也。
sentences.literal: When Yuan-di's aunt the Village Mistress of Guangchang died—not yet buried—Palace Assistant Xiong Yuan memorialized, stating: "I investigate the Rites: 'Toward ministers and great officers, until burial the ruler eats no meat; until the end of staged wailing he performs no music'—because the heart of compassion cannot bear to conduct auspicious affairs."
sentences.idiomatic: When Yuan-di's aunt, the Village Mistress of Guangchang, died and lay unburied, Palace Assistant Xiong Yuan submitted: "The Rites teach that until burial the ruler eats no meat for his ministers and until the end of staged wailing performs no music—because lingering pity forbids auspicious display."

sentences.chinese: 被尚書符，冬至後二日小會。
sentences.literal: We have received a Ministry tally—calling a minor gathering two days after the winter solstice.
sentences.idiomatic: Yet we have received a Ministry directive calling a minor court gathering two days after the winter solstice.

sentences.chinese: 臣以為廣昌鄉君喪殯日，聖恩垂悼。
sentences.literal: Your subject holds that on the encoffining days of the Village Mistress of Guangchang—sagely grace already hangs over her grief.
sentences.idiomatic: I hold that while the lady still lies in mourning hall, imperial sympathy already attends her.

sentences.chinese: 禮，大夫死，廢一時之祭。
sentences.literal: By ritual, when a great officer dies—one seasonal sacrifice is suspended.
sentences.idiomatic: Ritual suspends one seasonal sacrifice when a great officer dies.

sentences.chinese: 祭猶可廢，而況餘事。
sentences.literal: Sacrifices may still be suspended—how much more other affairs.
sentences.idiomatic: If even sacrifices may halt, how much more lesser observances.

sentences.chinese: 冬至唯可群下奉賀而已，未便小會。
sentences.literal: At the winter solstice it is only fitting that hosts below offer congratulations—that is all—not yet fitting to hold a minor gathering.
sentences.idiomatic: The solstice should bring nothing beyond congratulations from officials; a banquet is premature.

sentences.chinese: 」詔以遠表示賀循，又曰：「武皇帝故事云『王公大臣薨，三朝發哀，逾月不舉樂，其一朝發哀，三日不舉樂』，此舊事明文。
sentences.literal: The edict forwarded Xiong Yuan's memorial to He Xun and added: "Emperor Wu's precedent states: 'When kings, dukes, or great ministers die—three audiences of mourning—for more than a month no music is raised—those with one audience of mourning—for three days no music is raised'—this old affair has clear wording.
sentences.idiomatic: The throne forwarded Xiong Yuan's memorial to He Xun and added: "Emperor Wu's precedent reads: 'When kings, dukes, or great ministers die, three audiences of mourning mean no music for more than a month; a single audience means three days without music'—that ancient ruling is explicit.

sentences.chinese: 」賀循答曰：「案《禮·雜記》，『君于卿大夫之喪，比葬不食肉，比卒哭不舉樂』。
sentences.literal: He Xun answered, stating: "I investigate the Miscellaneous Record of the Rites: 'For the bereavement of ministers and great officers—until burial the ruler eats no meat—until the end of staged wailing he performs no music.'"
sentences.idiomatic: He Xun replied: "The Miscellaneous Record of the Rites says: 'For the death of ministers and great officers the ruler eats no meat until burial and performs no music until the end of staged wailing.'"

sentences.chinese: 古者君臣義重，雖以至尊之義，降而無服，三月之內，猶錫衰以居，不接吉事。
sentences.literal: In antiquity the righteousness between lord and minister was weighty—although by the utmost-venerated ritual principle mourning was lowered so there was no garment—within three months—smooth sackcloth was still worn at court—auspicious affairs were not joined.
sentences.idiomatic: Antiquity weighted the bond between ruler and minister so heavily that even when ritual "lowered" mourning to none, the sovereign still wore smooth sackcloth for three months and kept clear of joyous business.

sentences.chinese: 故春秋晉大夫智悼子未葬，平公作樂，為屠蒯所譏。
sentences.literal: Therefore in the Spring and Autumn annals, when the Jin great officer Zhi Daozi was not yet buried—Duke Ping ordered music—and was ridiculed by Tu Kuai.
sentences.idiomatic: Hence in the Spring and Autumn annals, when Duke Ping of Jin ordered music while Minister Zhi Daozi still lay unburied, Tu Kuai rebuked him.

sentences.chinese: 如遠所答，合于古義。
sentences.literal: As Xiong Yuan answered—it matches ancient righteousness.
sentences.idiomatic: Xiong Yuan's argument answers to classical meaning.

sentences.chinese: 咸寧詔書雖不會經典，然隨時立宜，以為定制，誠非群下所得稱論。
sentences.literal: Although the Xiánning edict document does not tally with the classics—yet it established what fitted its time—making it fixed regulation—truly not something hosts below may weigh and debate.
sentences.idiomatic: The Xiánning edict may not tally with every canonical line, yet it was framed for its moment and has become binding statute—not something subordinates may debate away.

sentences.chinese: 」，帝姑廬陵公主未葬，符問太常，冬至小會應作樂不。
sentences.literal: When the emperor's aunt the Princess of Luling was not yet buried—a tally asked the Grand Master of Ceremonies whether at the winter solstice minor gathering music ought to be performed.
sentences.idiomatic: Later, while the emperor's aunt, the Princess of Luling, remained unburied, a directive asked the Grand Master of Ceremonies whether music should sound at the winter-solstice gathering.

sentences.chinese: 博士胡訥議云：「君于卿大夫，比卒哭不舉樂。
sentences.literal: Erudite Hu Ne deliberated, stating: "Toward ministers and great officers—until the end of staged wailing music is not raised.
sentences.idiomatic: Erudite Hu Ne argued: "Until the end of staged wailing the ruler performs no music for ministers and great officers.

sentences.chinese: 公主有骨肉之親，宜闕樂。
sentences.literal: The princess has bone-and-flesh kinship—music fittingly should be omitted.
sentences.idiomatic: A princess is flesh and blood; music should be withheld.

sentences.chinese: 」太常王彪之云：「案武帝詔，三朝舉哀，三旬乃舉樂；
sentences.literal: Grand Master Wang Biaozhi stated: "I investigate Emperor Wu's edict—three audiences of mourning—for three ten-day cycles then music is raised;
sentences.idiomatic: Wang Biaozhi of the Grand Master office countered: "Emperor Wu's edict says three audiences of mourning delay music for three decadal cycles;

sentences.chinese: 其一朝舉哀者，三日則舉樂。
sentences.literal: those with one audience of mourning—after three days then music is raised.
sentences.idiomatic: a single audience lifts the ban after three days.

sentences.chinese: 春，長樂長公主薨，秋，扶風王駿薨，武帝並舉哀三日而已。
sentences.literal: In spring the Elder Princess of Changle died—in autumn Prince Jun of Fufeng died—Emperor Wu together observed mourning three days only.
sentences.idiomatic: In spring the Elder Princess of Changle died; in autumn Prince Jun of Fufeng died—Emperor Wu mourned each for three days only.

sentences.chinese: 中興已後，更參論不改此制。
sentences.literal: After the restoration—consultation and debate again did not alter this regulation.
sentences.idiomatic: Since the restoration the court has reviewed the matter repeatedly without changing that rule.

sentences.chinese: 今小會宜作樂。
sentences.literal: Now for the minor gathering it is fitting to perform music.
sentences.idiomatic: Music at today's gathering is therefore appropriate.

sentences.chinese: 」二議竟不知所取。
sentences.literal: In the end the two deliberations did not settle which to take.
sentences.idiomatic: The two opinions never settled which to follow.

sentences.chinese: 《喪服記》，公為所寓，齊衰三月。
sentences.literal: The Record of Mourning Dress: the duke for one who lodged him—trimmed sackcloth three months.
sentences.idiomatic: The Record of Mourning Dress says a duke wears three months of trimmed sackcloth for one who lodged him.

sentences.chinese: 新禮以今無此事，除此一章。
sentences.literal: The New Rites, because today this affair does not occur—removed this one chapter.
sentences.idiomatic: The New Rites dropped the chapter, judging the case obsolete.

sentences.chinese: 摯虞以為：「《周禮》作于刑厝之時，而著荒政十二。
sentences.literal: Zhi Yu deemed: "The Rites of Zhou were composed when punishments lay dormant—yet they record twelve famine-relief policies.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhi Yu argued: "The Rites of Zhou were compiled when punishments lay dormant, yet they still codified twelve relief measures for famine.

sentences.chinese: 禮備制待物，不以時衰而除盛典，世隆而闕衰教也。
sentences.literal: Ritual completes regulations to await things—not because the age declines thereby removing grand ceremonies—nor because the age is lofty thereby omitting mourning teaching.
sentences.idiomatic: Ritual completes institutions to meet every contingency; one does not strike great ceremonies merely because the age declines, nor abandon mourning instruction merely because the age flourishes.

sentences.chinese: 曩者王司徒失守播越，自稱寄公。
sentences.literal: Formerly Minister Wang lost his defense and was scattered in flight—calling himself a lodged duke.
sentences.idiomatic: Once Minister Wang lost his command and fled, styling himself a guest lord.

sentences.chinese: 是時天下又多此比，皆禮之所及。
sentences.literal: At that time all under heaven again had many of this sort—all are what ritual reaches.
sentences.idiomatic: Many in the realm stood in like case—precisely what ritual addresses.

sentences.chinese: 宜定新禮自如舊經。
sentences.literal: It is fitting to fix the New Rites to accord with the old classics.
sentences.idiomatic: The New Rites ought to be settled to match the old canon.

sentences.chinese: 」詔從之。
sentences.literal: The edict followed him.
sentences.idiomatic: An edict accepted his view.

sentences.chinese: 漢魏故事無五等諸侯之制，公卿朝士服喪，親疏各如其親。
sentences.literal: Han and Wei precedent lacked the institution of five-ranked feudal lords—dukes, ministers, and court gentlemen observed mourning—near or distant each according to actual kin.
sentences.idiomatic: Han and Wei precedent knew no five-tier nobility; dukes, ministers, and courtiers mourned according to actual kinship.

sentences.chinese: 新禮王公五等諸侯成國置卿者，及朝廷公孤之爵，皆傍親絕期，而旁親為之服斬衰，卿校位從大夫者皆絕緦。
sentences.literal: The New Rites: kings, dukes, five-ranked feudal lords who completed a state and installed ministers—and court ranks of duke and orphan—all collateral kin sever one-year mourning—yet collateral kin for them wear deepest mourning—ministerial officers whose rank follows great officers all sever finest-hemp mourning.
sentences.idiomatic: The New Rites would cut collateral ties at one year for kings, dukes, and five-tier lords who founded states with ministers, and for dukes and orphans at court—yet demand those collaterals wear deepest mourning for them, and sever even finest-hemp mourning for ministerial officers ranked with great officers.

sentences.chinese: 摯虞以為：「古者諸侯君臨其國，臣諸父兄，今之諸侯未同于古。
sentences.literal: Zhi Yu deemed: "Ancient feudal lords lorded over their states—treating fathers and elder brothers as ministers—present feudal lords are not the same as antiquity.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhi Yu argued: "Ancient feudal lords truly ruled their domains and treated uncles and elder brothers as ministers; today's nobles are not their peers.

sentences.chinese: 未同于古，則其尊未全，不宜便從絕期之制，而令傍親服斬衰之重也。
sentences.literal: Not the same as antiquity—then their honored standing is not complete—not fitting abruptly to follow the regulation that severs one-year mourning—yet order collateral kin to wear the weight of deepest mourning.
sentences.idiomatic: Because they lack that stature, their ritual supremacy is incomplete; they should not abruptly adopt the rule that severs one-year mourning while forcing collaterals into deepest mourning for them.

sentences.chinese: 諸侯既然，則公孤之爵亦宜如舊。
sentences.literal: Since feudal lords are thus—then ranks of duke and orphan also fittingly should be as before.
sentences.idiomatic: The same holds for dukes and orphans; let them follow earlier practice.

sentences.chinese: 昔魏武帝建安中已曾表上，漢朝依古為制，事與古異，皆不施行，施行者著在魏科。
sentences.literal: Formerly Emperor Wu of Wei in the Jiàn'ān era already once memorialized upward—the Han court according to antiquity made regulation—the affairs differed from antiquity—all were not enacted—what was enacted is recorded in Wei statutes.
sentences.idiomatic: Long ago Emperor Wu of Wei petitioned in the Jiàn'an era; Han tried to legislate on classical lines, found the cases unlike antiquity, and let the scheme lapse—what survived entered Wei law.

sentences.chinese: 大晉采以著令，宜定新禮皆如舊。
sentences.literal: Great Jin adopted this to establish ordinance—it is fitting to fix the New Rites entirely as the old.
sentences.idiomatic: Great Jin incorporated those provisions; the New Rites should be reset to match them.

sentences.chinese: 」詔從之。
sentences.literal: The edict followed him.
sentences.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.chinese: 《喪服》無弟子為師服之制，新禮弟子為師齊衰三月。
sentences.literal: Mourning Dress lacks any regulation for disciples mourning teachers—the New Rites prescribed disciples mourning teachers trimmed sackcloth three months.
sentences.idiomatic: Mourning Dress prescribes no mourning for a teacher; the New Rites imposed three months of trimmed sackcloth.

sentences.chinese: 摯虞以為：「自古無師服之制，故仲尼之喪，門人疑于所服。
sentences.literal: Zhi Yu deemed: "From antiquity there has been no regulation for mourning teachers—therefore at Zhongni's bereavement disciples doubted what to wear.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhi Yu noted that antiquity fixed no teacher-mourning; hence Confucius's disciples puzzled over what to wear.

sentences.chinese: 子貢曰：『昔夫子之喪顏回，若喪子而無服，請喪夫子若喪父而無服。
sentences.literal: Zigong stated: 'Formerly when the Master mourned Yan Hui—it was like mourning a son yet without garments—I request mourning the Master like mourning a father yet without garments.
sentences.idiomatic: Zigong said, 'When the Master mourned Yan Hui he grieved like a father yet wore no mourning dress; I ask to mourn the Master as I would a father but likewise without prescribed garments.'

sentences.chinese: 』遂心喪三年。
sentences.literal: ' Thereupon they observed heart-mourning three years.
sentences.idiomatic: ' They therefore observed three years of heart-mourning.

sentences.chinese: 此則懷三年之哀，而無齊衰之制也。
sentences.literal: This then cherishes three years of grief—yet lacks the trimmed-sackcloth regulation.
sentences.idiomatic: Thus they bore three years of grief without the formal trimmed-sackcloth regimen.

sentences.chinese: 群居，入則絰，出則否，所謂弔服加麻也。
sentences.literal: Dwelling in a group—entering then cord—exiting then not—this is what is called condolence garb with hemp added.
sentences.idiomatic: Living together, they donned hemp cords indoors and doffed them outdoors—the so-called mourning garb with added hemp.

sentences.chinese: 先聖為禮，必易從而可傳。
sentences.literal: Former sages made ritual—it must be easy to follow and possible to transmit.
sentences.idiomatic: The sages fashioned ritual to be easy to follow and easy to hand down.

sentences.chinese: 師徒義誠重，而服制不著，歷代相襲，不以為缺。
sentences.literal: Teacher and disciple righteousness is truly heavy—yet garment regulation is not manifest—successive ages mutually inherited—not deeming it a deficiency.
sentences.idiomatic: Master and pupil mean much, yet no mourning wardrobe was codified; dynasty after dynasty accepted the silence without calling it a flaw.

sentences.chinese: 且尋師者以彌高為得，故屢遷而不嫌；
sentences.literal: Moreover those who seek teachers take ever higher attainment as gain—therefore they shift repeatedly without dislike;
sentences.idiomatic: Seekers of teachers prize ever loftier instruction, so they change masters without shame;

sentences.chinese: 修業者以日新為益，故舍舊而不疑。
sentences.literal: those who cultivate learning take daily renewal as benefit—therefore they abandon the old without hesitation.
sentences.idiomatic: students who pursue improvement welcome each day's novelty and leave former teachers without hesitation.

sentences.chinese: 仲尼稱『三人行，必有我師焉』。
sentences.literal: Zhongni praised 'Three persons walking—there must be my teacher therein.'
sentences.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'In any trio walking by, there is surely my teacher.'

sentences.chinese: 子貢云，『夫何常師之有』。
sentences.literal: Zigong stated—'Now what fixed teacher is there?'
sentences.idiomatic: Zigong added, 'Who keeps one fixed master forever?'

sentences.chinese: 淺學之師，暫學之師，不可皆為之服。
sentences.literal: Teachers of shallow learning—teachers of brief learning—not possible for all to observe mourning for them.
sentences.idiomatic: Casual tutors and brief instructors cannot all merit full mourning dress.

sentences.chinese: 義有輕重，服有廢興，則臧否由之而起，是非因之而爭，愛惡相攻，悔吝生焉。
sentences.literal: When righteousness has light and heavy—and garments have abandonment and revival—then praise and blame arise thereby—right and wrong contend thereby—love and hate attack each other—regret and shame are born therein.
sentences.idiomatic: Where obligation varies and garments rise or fall, praise and blame ignite, right and wrong quarrel, liking and loathing clash, and regret follows.

sentences.chinese: 宜定新禮無服如舊。
sentences.literal: It is fitting to fix the New Rites—no garments—as the old.
sentences.idiomatic: The New Rites should revert to the old silence—no prescribed mourning.

sentences.chinese: 」詔從之。
sentences.literal: The edict followed him.
sentences.idiomatic: An edict agreed.

sentences.chinese: 古者天子諸侯葬禮粗備，漢世又多變革，魏晉以下世有改變，大體同漢之制。
sentences.literal: In antiquity Son of Heaven and feudal lords' burial rites were roughly complete—the Han age again had many changes—from Wei and Jin downward generations had alterations—the great outline largely matched Han regulation.
sentences.idiomatic: Antiquity gave Son of Heaven and nobles a rough burial code; Han reworked it often; Wei and Jin kept tweaking, yet the outline still followed Han.

sentences.chinese: 而魏武以禮送終之制，襲稱之數，繁而無益，俗又過之，豫自制送終衣服四篋，題識其上，春秋冬夏，日有不諱，隨時以斂。
sentences.literal: Yet Emperor Wu of Wei deemed ritual regulations for sending off the dead—the inherited titles and tallies—numerous yet without benefit—custom again surpassed them—beforehand he himself made send-off garments four chests—inscribed marks on their tops—spring, autumn, winter, summer—when the day held no taboo—following the season thereby to encoffin.
sentences.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Wei judged funeral ritual bloated with pointless inherited titles; popular excess made it worse. He prepared four chests of burial clothes in advance, labeled them for the seasons, and ordered that whenever death came, whatever the season, he be dressed from those stores.

sentences.chinese: 金珥珠玉銅鐵之物，一不得送。
sentences.literal: Things of gold ear-rings pearl jade copper iron—not one may be sent along.
sentences.idiomatic: Not a single article of gold, jeweled earpieces, jade, copper, or iron might accompany him.

sentences.chinese: 文帝遵奉，無所增加。
sentences.literal: Emperor Wen obeyed and upheld—nothing was increased.
sentences.idiomatic: Emperor Wen adhered without adding.

sentences.chinese: 及受禪，刻金璽，追加尊號，不敢開埏，乃為石室，藏璽埏首，以示陵中無金銀諸物也。
sentences.literal: When it came to receiving the abdication—a gold seal was carved—posthumous honor was added—he dared not open the tomb slope—thereupon made a stone chamber—hid the seal at the tomb-head—to show that inside the mausoleum there were no gold or silver objects.
sentences.idiomatic: After accepting the abdication he had a gold seal cut and posthumous honors added, yet feared opening the slope; he built a stone niche at the entrance and sealed the cipher there to show the mound held no gold or silver.

sentences.chinese: 漢禮明器甚多，自是皆省之矣。
sentences.literal: Han ritual spirit-objects were very many—from this onward all were reduced.
sentences.idiomatic: Han tombs had brimmed with grave goods; from then on those were pared back.

sentences.chinese: 魏文帝，又自作終制曰：「禮，國君即位為椑，存不忘亡也。
sentences.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei—again himself composed end instructions stating: "Ritual—a state lord at accession makes the inner coffin—existing does not forget perishing.
sentences.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei also drafted final instructions: "Ritual demands that a ruler have his inner coffin readied at accession—the living must remember dying.

sentences.chinese: 壽陵因山為體，無封樹，無立寢殿，造園邑，通神道。
sentences.literal: The Shou mausoleum relies on the mountain as its body—no mound or trees—no erecting resting halls—building garden settlements—opening spirit roads.
sentences.idiomatic: My barrow at Shou will hug the hill without mound-markers or trees, without resting halls, garden towns, or spirit ways cut through.

sentences.chinese: 夫葬者藏也，欲人之不得見也。
sentences.literal: Now burial is hiding—it desires that people not obtain sight.
sentences.idiomatic: Burial means concealment; it must hide the dead from sight.

sentences.chinese: 禮不墓祭，欲存亡不黷也。
sentences.literal: Ritual does not sacrifice at the tomb—it desires that neither the living nor the dead be profaned.
sentences.idiomatic: Ritual forbids tomb-side sacrifice so neither living nor dead suffer violation.

sentences.chinese: 皇后及貴人以下不隨王之國者，有終沒，皆葬澗西，前又已表其處矣。
sentences.literal: Empresses and honored ladies below who do not follow the prince to his state—when they end and die—all are buried west of the stream—I have already earlier marked their place.
sentences.idiomatic: Empresses and concubines who do not travel to princely domains will, when they die, all be buried west of the stream—I have already noted the site.

sentences.chinese: 」此詔藏之宗廟，副在尚書、秘書、三府。
sentences.literal: This edict store it in the ancestral temple—copies at the Ministry, the Palace Library, and the Three Offices.
sentences.idiomatic: He ordered this edict deposited in the ancestral shrine with copies at the Secretariat, the Palace Library, and the three chief ministries.

sentences.chinese: 明帝亦遵奉之。
sentences.literal: Mingdi also obeyed and upheld it.
sentences.idiomatic: Mingdi likewise obeyed.

sentences.chinese: 明帝性雖崇奢，然未遽營陵墓之制也。
sentences.literal: Although Mingdi's nature esteemed extravagance—yet he did not hastily undertake expanding mausoleum-hill regulation.
sentences.idiomatic: Though Mingdi loved splendor, he still refrained from rashly expanding tomb ritual.

sentences.chinese: 宣帝豫自于首陽山為土藏，不填不樹，作《顧命終制》，斂以時服，不設明器。
sentences.literal: Emperor Xuan beforehand on Mount Shouyang made an earthen store—no filling mound no trees—composed the Testamentary Resting Instructions—encoffined in timely garments—did not install spirit-objects.
sentences.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan prepared an earthen repository at Mount Shouyang—no raised mound, no marker trees—writing his Testamentary Resting Instructions to be dressed in daily clothes and buried without grave goods.
